summary: Late-handshake backlog causing apigw 5xx spike and upstream runtime preemption under tenant CPU pressure
description: Issue summary: Customers (notably Waveform Analytics, dedicated tenant) observed a sudden elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway beginning 2026-03-12 20:13 UTC. Errors coincide with long TLS/ALPN handshake latencies and a subsequent cascade of runtime preemptions / supervisor restarts for serving-runtime processes assigned to the tenant. Impact: ~18% of requests returned 502/503 over a 25-minute window for the tenant; overall cluster error rate increased by ~3% during the window. Visible customer-facing symptoms: streaming sessions dropped mid-response, and bulk embedding uploads intermittently failed with 5xx. Timeline: - 2026-03-12 20:09 UTC: minor increase in ALPN negotiation latencies on a subset of edge proxies. - 20:13 UTC: api-gateway 5xx rate begins to rise; keepalive pool consumption increases. - 20:18 UTC: serving-runtime supervisors report CPU scheduling delays; OOM-like preemptions observed for tenant worker groups (preempt -> restart). - 20:32 UTC: mitigation actions (accept-queue increase, temporary rate limit applied for tenant) reduce error rate. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation and follow-ups.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate sustained concurrent streaming + embedding workload from a single dedicated tenant (Waveform-like traffic profile: 40 concurrent streams + 8 embedding uploads).
2) Use HTTP/2 with ALPN; include TLS session reuse on long-lived connections.
3) Ramp concurrency over 5 minutes and observe accept queue, TLS handshake latencies, and runtime supervisor metrics.
4) Observe apigw 502/503 when handshake backlog + CPU contention align.

investigation_notes: Hypotheses considered: 1) ALPN/TLS handshake queuing on edge proxies caused long tail latencies -> backpressure to runtime. 2) Keepalive connection reuse semantics combined with HTTP/2 stream multiplexing caused head-of-line blocking. 3) The serving-runtime preemption logic misinterpreted high CPU scheduling latencies as hung workers and forcibly restarted them, amplifying failure rate. Findings: - Heatmap of alpn_neg shows a spike on edge nodes colocated with tenant's egress IPs. - Kernel-level tcp_tw_reuse and TCP backlog exhaustion correlated with accept queue growth. - Supervisor logs show preempt_count spikes tied to cpu_wait_ms > 1500. - No OOMs in dmesg; restarts were preemption-based by our watchdog (we killed workers to break perceived deadlocks). - A recent change in the edge-proxy TLS handshake loop (PR #241) introduced a tighter retry delay which increases active TLS worker retention under high backlog. Partial replication in staging: reproduced when artificially limiting ephemeral worker counts on proxies and simultaneously running cpu-heavy model in the runtime.
comments: 2026-03-12 20:24 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified customer (Waveform) of elevated errors; applied temporary tenant-level rate limit to reduce tail pressure.
2026-03-12 20:42 UTC - SRE (Liam): Increased apigw accept_queue and bumped proxy ephemeral workers by +30% on affected hosts; error rate falling.
2026-03-13 09:15 UTC - Eng (Priya Ghosh): Reproduced in staging with scripted ALPN stall; PR identified that increases handshake worker lifetime under retry path (edge-proxy PR #241).
2026-03-13 11:02 UTC - Runtime (Marco): Watchdog preemption threshold adjusted in staging; reduced forced restarts for cpu_wait_ms < 3000 to avoid cascades.
2026-03-14 07:30 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed services stabilized after mitigations; provided notes for post-incident review.
resolution: Mitigated: - Edge proxies rolled back the handshake retry delay change from PR #241 on affected hosts (rollback tag v2.3.7->v2.3.6). - Temporarily increased accept_queue and ephemeral TLS worker pool on egress-edge nodes in us-east-1. - Applied tenant rate limit for Waveform to protect shared capacity during remediation window. - Adjusted runtime watchdog preemption threshold to be more permissive for short CPU stalls. Permanent fix plan: optimize handshake retry backoff logic to prevent worker retention, introduce connection-shed behavior prior to forced runtime preemption, and add heuristics to correlate apigw backlog with runtime restarts.
